body:
Cold presence recovery currently holds a coarse hash lane across owner I/O. An unrelated cold UID in that lane can wait behind the first request despite having its own authority proof to recover. Replace lane ownership with exact UID and distributed-authority flights, publish newly owned proofs before joining prior flights, and preserve Directory fencing, eviction semantics, existing retries and the four-call owner gate.

Admission is bounded to four leader cohorts, 2,048 retained keys and 128 MiB of registry-owned UID clones, with 32 MiB per newly owned subset. The original 512-UID/256-target packing fits maximum stored identities; oversized arbitrary cold lookup strings return typed not-ready. Flights retain status rather than routes, and successful callers reread Directory.

Also identify metadata-checkpoint finalization rejections through closed diagnostic reasons while preserving accounting, retry/deadline behavior, incomplete-report failures and prior product observations. This diagnostic change does not repair or reclassify the previously invalid report.

Validation:
- Tests-first controlled isolation regressions: old implementation produced 13 behavioral failures; the unchanged focused tests pass after the change.
- Complete presence/runtime packages pass normally and under race (106 test events each); four production owner-adapter recovery contracts pass under race.
- Complete chat-lifecycle/CLI benchmark packages pass (871 top-level tests / 1,685 test events); focused diagnostic race checks pass.
- Named formatting/FLOW checks pass. Independent Standards and Spec reviews have no remaining findings; the initial P3 documentation clarification and its closure are retained.
- Exact-source native process diagnostic retained the same 10,000-user/2,000-group distribution, seed, 500 SEND/s config and gates. It still failed: terminal SEND=ACK 10,502, zero first-attempt failures/rejections, one sampled expiry. Finalization is now specifically `meta_checkpoint/metrics_fetch`; CLI remains harness-invalid, exit 8, with no final report. All owned processes and 64 ports were cleared. This validates neither a loss fix nor the full 120-second window; the cloud rehearsal root cause remains open.

The released cloud rehearsal had message loss and remains unqualified. This PR does not publish a release or authorize another paid run.
